hypotheses.title: Net Liquid Cash Solvency Ratio (cash_st - debt_st over assets)
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Financial distress and refinancing risk create severe asymmetric downside for leveraged corporations. In credit tightening cycles, companies with positive net liquid cash (cash_st - debt_st) have zero debt rollover risk, earn attractive yield on cash reserves, and possess opportunistic capital to execute share buybacks. Conversely, firms where short-term debt exceeds liquid cash face acute refinancing and insolvency pressure. Standardizing net liquid cash by total assets across a 1-year time-series range isolates pristine corporate solvency, generating consistent alpha with 100% universal instrument coverage and turnover in the 10-14% sweet spot.
confounders: Sudden speculative rallies in high-debt distress equities driven by debt restructuring relief
hypotheses.falsification_test: Fails if high net cash firms underperform net debtor firms within subindustries.

hypotheses.title: Corporate Capital Expenditure Discipline vs Empire Building (-capex over assets)
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Empirical asset pricing research (Titman, Wei, Xie 2004; Cooper, Gulen, Schill 2008) documents that corporate managers frequently overinvest free cash flow into negative-NPV pet projects and dilutive empire building, destroying shareholder value. Firms demonstrating capital expenditure discipline relative to their asset base (-capex / assets) generate higher return on invested capital and superior shareholder returns. Evaluating capex intensity against a 1-year baseline isolates firms expanding margins through capital discipline.
confounders: Rapid technological transitions where aggressive capital expenditure expansion is necessary to avoid obsolescence
hypotheses.falsification_test: Fails if high-capex empire builders systematically outperform capital-disciplined firms over multi-year cycles.

hypotheses.title: Core Operating Asset Productivity (Novy-Marx Gross Profitability / ROC) (ebit over assets)
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Novy-Marx (2013) demonstrated that asset productivity (ebit / assets) is the purest measure of true economic profitability, unclouded by discretionary depreciation or leverage. While price-scaled ratios (ebit / close) suffer from price-momentum feedback loops, scaling operating earnings by the firm's productive asset base identifies true economic moats. Measuring trailing 1-year time-series rank (ts_rank(..., 252)) within each subindustry captures improving asset utilization with ultra-low turnover.
confounders: Asset-light software or IP-heavy businesses where balance-sheet assets understate true productive capacity
hypotheses.falsification_test: Fails if high asset productivity firms underperform low-productivity peers within the same subindustry.
